enriched_description: Soft-bodied invertebrate worm exhibiting dorsoventrally flattened leaf-like or ribbon-like body shape measuring 1 mm to 60 cm in length depending on species. Body displays bilateral symmetry with distinct anterior head region bearing eyespots (ocelli) and chemoreceptive auricles. Surface texture is smooth, moist, and ciliated, ranging in color from translucent white to brown, grey, or black. No body cavity (acoelomate) present. Locomotion via ciliary gliding or muscular undulations creating characteristic rippling motion. Body is unsegmented with simple digestive system featuring single opening. Free-living species display triangular or arrow-shaped head; parasitic forms are elongated and segmented (tapeworms).

Microscopic to small unsegmented worm with elongated cylindrical body tapering to fine points at both anterior and posterior ends, measuring 0.3 mm to 8 cm in length. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with smooth, flexible cuticle covering, appearing translucent white, cream, or pale yellow under magnification. Cross-section reveals round (not flattened) body plan distinguishing from flatworms. Head region bears sensory amphids and labial papillae. Locomotion via characteristic thrashing or sinusoidal undulations due to longitudinal muscles only. Body cavity is pseudocoelomate. Mouth opening may feature stylet in plant-parasitic species. Surface texture is smooth and glossy.

Large marine gastropod mollusk with distinctive brightly-colored spiral shell measuring 15-30 cm in length. Shell exhibits dextral (right-handed) coiling with prominent flared outer lip, often orange, pink, or brown with spiral ridges and nodular projections. Aperture is large and elongated with characteristic siphonal canal extending anteriorly. Shell surface displays glossy calcareous texture with spiral growth lines. Soft body extends from aperture featuring large muscular foot for locomotion, paired eyestalks, and siphon for water intake. Operculum is claw-shaped and corneous. Shell interior exhibits pearlescent pink to white coloration. Weight ranges 1-5 kg.

Gastropod mollusk with soft unsegmented body protected by external spiral shell coiled in helical pattern. Shell varies from 2 mm to 75 cm depending on species, exhibiting dextral or sinistral coiling with coloration ranging from brown, tan, yellow to banded patterns. Shell surface texture ranges from smooth and glossy to ribbed or granulated. Soft body extends from shell aperture featuring broad muscular foot for gliding locomotion, leaving characteristic mucous trail. Head bears two pairs of tentacles: upper pair with eyes at tips, lower pair for olfaction. Mantle secretes shell material. Body is moist, soft, and bilaterally symmetrical internally despite external asymmetry.

Terrestrial gastropod mollusk with elongated soft body lacking external shell, measuring 2-25 cm in length. Body surface is smooth, moist, and covered with protective mucus layer giving glossy slimy appearance. Coloration ranges from grey, brown, black, yellow, to orange, often with darker longitudinal stripes or mottled patterns. Dorsal mantle is visible as saddle-shaped structure on anterior third of body, sometimes containing reduced internal shell remnant. Head bears two pairs of retractable tentacles with eyes at tips of upper pair. Muscular foot extends entire ventral length for gliding locomotion. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with soft, flexible texture. Leaves characteristic silvery mucous trail.

Marine gastropod mollusk with shell-less body exhibiting vibrant coloration and elaborate external appendages. Body is elongated and soft, measuring 1-30 cm, displaying brilliant hues of blue, purple, orange, yellow, green, or red, often with contrasting patterns and spots. Dorsal surface features prominent cerata (finger-like projections) or flattened notal plates used for respiration and defense. Cerata are translucent to opaque, often tipped with contrasting colors. Head bears oral tentacles and rhinophores (sensory structures) that are feathery or club-shaped. Mantle is reduced or absent. Body texture is smooth, gelatinous, and delicate. Locomotion via muscular foot or swimming undulations. Many species exhibit aposematic coloration warning of toxicity.

Primitive marine mollusk with elongated oval bilaterally symmetrical body measuring 2-35 cm in length. Dorsal surface is protected by eight overlapping calcareous plates (valves) arranged in linear series from anterior to posterior. Plates are embedded in tough leathery girdle (mantle) that may be smooth, spiny, or hairy depending on species. Plate coloration ranges from grey, brown, green to mottled patterns with textured surface showing growth lines. Ventral surface features broad muscular foot for adhesion to rocky substrates. Head is reduced without eyes or tentacles. Body exhibits dorsoventrally flattened profile when clinging to surfaces. Texture is hard and armored dorsally, soft and muscular ventrally. Can curl into defensive ball when dislodged.

Marine cephalopod mollusk with distinctive external spiral shell measuring 15-25 cm in diameter. Shell exhibits planispiral coiling in single plane with 30+ internal chambers separated by pale pearly septa visible as sutures on exterior. Outer shell surface is smooth, glossy, and white with radial brown or reddish-brown stripes radiating from apex. Shell interior displays iridescent nacreous (mother-of-pearl) finish. Soft body emerges from shell aperture featuring 60-90 retractable tentacles arranged in two circles around mouth, lacking suckers. Eyes are simple pits without lenses. Funnel (hyponome) is used for jet propulsion. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry. Shell provides buoyancy control through gas-filled chambers.

Medium-sized edible decapod crustacean with broad oval carapace measuring 15-23 cm in width. Carapace is smooth and convex, displaying purplish-brown to reddish-brown coloration with lighter mottled patterns. Ventral surface is cream to white. Five pairs of walking legs extend laterally with first pair modified into robust claws (chelipeds) of unequal size. Claws are dark-tipped with smooth outer surface and serrated inner edges. Eyes are stalked and protrude from anterior carapace margin. Abdomen (tail) is folded ventrally, broad in females, narrow in males. Exoskeleton is hard and calcified with smooth glossy texture. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry. Weight ranges 0.5-1.5 kg.

Medium-sized decapod crustacean with broad rounded carapace measuring 6-12 cm in width. Carapace exhibits smooth convex surface with distinctive purple-brown to reddish-brown coloration, often with darker mottling and lighter margins. Ventral surface is pale cream to yellowish. Five pairs of walking legs are relatively short and robust compared to body width. Claws (chelipeds) are stout and unequal in size with dark brown to black tips and smooth outer surface. Eyes are stalked and positioned at anterior carapace corners. Abdomen is folded ventrally with segmented structure visible in juveniles. Exoskeleton is hard, calcified, and glossy. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry. Distinguished from Dungeness crab by smaller size and more rounded carapace shape.
